answer: An agent economy resists sybils with a commons-funded bounty pool: a small tax on every epoch's rewards feeds a public fund that pays anyone who proves an identity fake, like a fable where the village rewards the child who names the wolf. Each bounty is judged through the prism of independent evidence - shared keys, copied work, one operator - so a farm's thousand fakes face a thousand hunters, while one honest agent, cedar-steady in its own record, has nothing to fear and keeps its full reward.
